citation: Xtreme Reading. (2011). Evidence for ESSA program review. https://www.evidenceforessa.org
title: Successful Xtreme Reading implementation requires leadership support for coaching time and accommodating school schedules
description: The review specifies that implementation depends on leadership that is "willing to support teachers in implementation, provide time for coaching, and willing to create school schedules that accommodate such instruction." This reflects the program's highly structured methods, which need both teacher willingness to follow instructional steps and organizational conditions that protect coaching and scheduling time.
requirements: Teachers willing and able to implement the instructional steps provided by the curriculum
examples: Site professional development is 5 days of instruction (3 in summer, 2 in fall), with monthly coaching, data collection, and instructional decision-making sessions
key_sources: Xtreme Reading. (2011). Evidence for ESSA program review. https://www.evidenceforessa.org

article_title: Preterm children's long-term academic performance after adaptive computerized training: an efficacy and process analysis of a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Jaekel Julia, Heuser Katharina M., Zapf Antonia, Roll Claudia, Nuñez Francisco Brevis, Bartmann Peter, Wolke Dieter, Feldhoff-Mueser Ursula, Huening Britta. (2020). Preterm children’s long-term academic performance after adaptive computerized training: an efficacy and process analysis of a randomized controlled trial. Pediatric Research. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41390-020-01114-w
title: XtraMath adaptive online math fact-fluency program
description: XtraMath is an online, computerized math program that "continuously adapts to children's abilities" and "aims to help students transition from counting or calculating the basic math facts to automatically recalling them." It uses timed activities with 3-s thresholds, spaced repetition, and four operation components (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division), each starting with a placement quiz that sets the individual mastery score. In this trial, preterm first graders used the standard protocol of at least 5×/weekly 10–15 min practice for 5 weeks, with only one-digit addition tasks (0 + 0 to 9 + 9), weekly parent progress emails, and coach support.
requirements: Daily home practice with parental supervision; a trained coach provided weekly in-person and phone-based technical and motivational support during the 5-week intervention period
constraints: In this study only one-digit addition tasks were used to standardize training content; the program is not language-dependent but instructions are available in nine languages
target_learning_goals: automatic recall of basic arithmetic facts (computational fluency)
examples: Preterm first graders completed at least 5×/weekly 10–15 min sessions for 5 weeks at home, progressing sequentially through operations based on mastery
